verses.zh: 以色列啊，你要归向耶和华―你的　神；你是因自己的罪孽跌倒了。
verses.en: Return, O Israel, to the Lord your God,for your sin has been your downfall![NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “For you have stumbled in your iniquity”; cf. NASB, NRSV “because of your iniquity.”

verses.zh: 当归向耶和华，用言语祷告他说：求你除净罪孽，悦纳善行；这样，我们就把嘴唇的祭代替牛犊献上。
verses.en: Return to the Lord and repent![NOTE:1] Say to him: “Completely[NOTE:2] forgive our iniquity;accept[NOTE:3] our penitential prayer,[NOTE:4] that we may offer the praise of our lips as sacrificial bulls.[NOTE:5]
notes: Heb “Take words with you and return to the Lord” (so NASB, NIV, NRSV).

The word order כָּל־תִּשָּׂא עָוֹן (kol tisaʾ ʿavon) is syntactically awkward. The BHS editors suggest rearranging the word order: תִּשָּׂא כָּל־עָוֹן (“Forgive all [our] iniquity!”). However, Gesenius suggests that כָּל (“all”) does not function as the construct in the genitive phrase כָּל־עָוֹן (“all [our] iniquity”); it functions adverbially modifying the verb תִּשָּׂא (“Completely forgive!”; see GKC 415 §128.e).

The repetition of the root לָקַח (laqakh) creates a striking wordplay in 14:2. If Israel will bring (לָקַח) its confession to God, he will accept (לָקַח) repentant Israel and completely forgive its sin.

Heb “and accept [our] speech.” The word טוֹב (tov) is often confused with the common homonymic root I טוֹב (tov, “good”; BDB 373 s.v. I טוֹב). However, this is probably IV טוֹב (tov, “word, speech”; HALOT 372 s.v. IV טוֹב), a hapax legomenon that is related to the verb טבב (“to speak”; HALOT 367 s.v. טבב) and the noun טִבָּה (tibbah, “rumor”; HALOT 367 s.v. טִבָּה). The term טוֹב (“word; speech”) refers to the repentant prayer mentioned in 14:1-3. Most translations relate it to I טוֹב and treat it as (1) accusative direct object: “accept that which is good” (RSV, NJPS) and “Accept our good sacrifices” (CEV), or (2) adverbial accusative of manner: “receive [us] graciously” (KJV, NASB, NIV). Note TEV, however, which follows the suggestion made here: “accept our prayer.”

The MT reads פָרִים (farim, “bulls”), but the LXX reflects פְּרִי (peri, “fruit”), a reading followed by NASB, NIV, NRSV “that we may offer the fruit of [our] lips [as sacrifices to you].” Although the Greek expression in Heb 13:15 (καρπὸν χειλέων, karpon cheileōn, “the fruit of lips”) reflects this LXX phrase, the MT makes good sense as it stands; NT usage of the LXX should not be considered decisive in resolving OT textual problems. The noun פָּרִים (parim, “bulls”) functions as an adverbial accusative of state.

verses.zh: 我们不向亚述求救，不骑埃及的马，也不再对我们手所造的说：你是我们的　神。因为孤儿在你―耶和华那里得蒙怜悯。
verses.en: Assyria cannot save us;we will not ride warhorses.We will never again say, ‘Our gods,’to what our own hands have made.For only you will show compassion to Orphan Israel!”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “For the orphan is shown compassion by you.” The present translation takes “orphan” as a figurative reference to Israel, which is specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 我必医治他们背道的病，甘心爱他们；因为我的怒气向他们转消。
verses.en: “I will heal their waywardness[NOTE:1] and love them freely,[NOTE:2] for my anger will turn away[NOTE:3] from them.
notes: The noun מְשׁוּבָתָה (meshuvatah, “waywardness”; cf. KJV “backsliding”) is from the same root as שׁוּבָה (shuvah, “return!”) in 14:1 [14:2 HT]. This repetition of שׁוּב (shuv) creates a wordplay that emphasizes reciprocity: if Israel will return (שׁוּבָה, shuvah) to the Lord, he will cure her of the tendency to turn away (מְשׁוּבָתָה) from him.

The noun נְדָבָה (nedavah, “voluntariness; free-will offering”) is an adverbial accusative of manner: “freely, voluntarily” (BDB 621 s.v. נְדָבָה 1). Cf. CEV “without limit,” TEV “with all my heart,” NLT “my love will know no bounds.”

The verb שָׁב, shav, “will turn” (Qal perfect third person masculine singular from שׁוּב, shuv, “to turn”), continues the wordplay on שׁוּב in 14:1-4 [14:2-5 HT]. If Israel will “return” (שׁוּב) to the Lord, he will heal Israel’s tendency to “turn away” (מְשׁוּבָתָה, meshuvatah) and “turn” (שָׁב) from his anger.

verses.zh: 我必向以色列如甘露；他必如百合花开放，如黎巴嫩的树木扎根。
verses.en: I will be like the dew to Israel;he will blossom like a lily;he will send down his roots like a cedar of[NOTE:1] Lebanon.
notes: Heb “like Lebanon” (so KJV; also in the following verse). The phrase “a cedar of” does not appear in the Hebrew text; it is supplied in translation for clarity (cf. TEV “the trees of Lebanon,” NRSV “the forests of Lebanon”).

verses.zh: 他的枝条必延长；他的荣华如橄榄树；他的香气如黎巴嫩的香柏树。
verses.en: His young shoots will grow;his splendor will be like an olive tree;his fragrance like a cedar of Lebanon.

verses.zh: 曾住在他荫下的必归回，发旺如五谷，开花如葡萄树。他的香气如黎巴嫩的酒。
verses.en: People will reside again[NOTE:1] in his shade;they will plant and harvest grain in abundance.[NOTE:2] They will blossom like a vine,and his fame will be like the wine from Lebanon.
notes: Hosea uses the similar-sounding terms יָשֻׁבוּ יֹשְׁבֵי (yashuvu yosheve, “the dwellers will return”) to create a wordplay between the roots שׁוּב (shuv, “to return”) and יָשַׁב (yashav, “to dwell; to reside”).

Heb “they will cause the grain to live” or “they will revive the grain.” Some English versions treat this as a comparison: “they shall revive as the corn,” (KJV) and “will flourish like the grain” (NIV).

verses.zh: 以法莲必说：我与偶像还有甚么关涉呢？我―耶和华回答他，也必顾念他。我如青翠的松树；你的果子从我而得。
verses.en: O Ephraim, I do not want to have anything to do[NOTE:1] with idols anymore!I will answer him and care for him.I am like[NOTE:2] a luxuriant cypress tree;[NOTE:3] your fruitfulness comes from me!”[NOTE:4]
notes: The Hebrew expression מַה־לִּי עוֹד (mah-lli ʿod) is a formula of repudiation/emphatic denial that God has anything in common with idols: “I want to have nothing to do with […] any more!” (cf., e.g., Judg 11:12; 2 Sam 16:10; 19:23; 1 Kgs 17:18; 2 Kgs 3:13; 2 Chr 35:21; Jer 2:18; Ps 50:16; BDB 553 s.v. מָה 1.d.[c]).
The term “like” does not appear in the Hebrew text but is supplied in the translation for clarity, as in the majority of English versions (including KJV).
Cf. KJV “a green fir tree,” NIV84, NCV “a green pine tree,” NIV11 “a flourishing juniper,” NRSV “an evergreen cypress.”
Heb “your fruit is found in me”; cf. NRSV “your faithfulness comes from me.”

verses.zh: 谁是智慧人？可以明白这些事；谁是通达人？可以知道这一切。因为，耶和华的道是正直的；义人必在其中行走，罪人却在其上跌倒。
verses.en: Who is wise? Let him discern[NOTE:1] these things!Who is discerning? Let him understand them!For the ways of the Lord are right;the godly walk in them,but in them the rebellious stumble.
notes: The shortened form of the prefix-conjugation verb וְיָבֵן (veyaven) indicates that it is a jussive rather than an imperfect. When a jussive comes from a superior to an inferior, it may connote exhortation and instruction or advice and counsel. For the functions of the jussive, see IBHS 568-70 §34.3.
